title: Memory, Projects, Styles, Feature Flags and configuration: source evidence

scope.mode: Official distributed ion-dist assets; inert analysis only; no target app execution, login, hidden-route requests, flag manipulation, profile or credential access
scope.code_claims: Conditional client implementation; not an authenticated runtime observation

facts.claim: Classic memory response parser accepts summary text, nullable string-array controls, timezone-normalized timestamp, optional project import and mode.
Classic reads are account/org/project scoped and gated by organization, caller enabled, feature, and policy status.
Classic controls PUT is distinct from summary synthesis POST; successful controls edit optionally chains synthesis then invalidates scoped cached data.
Reset POST and user disable/cache purge are distinct client actions; a settings switch does not by itself prove server deletion.
User gestures accept four exact key sets; clear_data is accepted only for master-off with both memory flags false.
Ordinary mutation strips user_initiated and clear_data; gesture mutation adds explicit user intent after validation.
Memory settings writes serialize per organization and recover the queue after failures; optimistic bootstrap fields are rolled back on error.
Successful settings response replaces the scoped settings cache and mode; write requests have a 30-second abort timeout.
Settings caches have explicit refresh budgets; a pre-start path can reread old settings and fail closed unless a held-value policy is explicitly selected.
facts.limits: These are client branch defaults, not observed request timings or product retention periods.

facts.claim: The memory resolver first uses a non-null/non-undefined server mode for memoryOn and a candidate mode; otherwise it derives a candidate from preference, flags and capability state. The returned UI mode then projects a saffron/classic candidate to melange when classic is unavailable and melange is available. The original value remains separately exposed as serverMemoryMode; blocked status is not equivalent to user pause.
Topic memory list and per-path reads use org-scoped cache keys and POST-backed query functions.
Topic delete removes its cached row and read query and updates probe counts. Reset cancels old queries before clearing list/probe/read state.
Topic edit is a streaming instruction request with optional path/model, not a local extractor implementation.
facts.limits: No extraction, retrieval ranking, server storage implementation, or model prompt ordering is recovered by this API call.

facts.claim: Topic edit cancels the previous request, versions UI state, ignores late aborted results, prefers authoritative server edit results, and reconciles a fresh list when parsing cannot establish mutations.
Topic import polls pending state at five seconds; switch-import has bounded 404/transient tolerance distinct from pending processing.
Local Cowork startup plumbing visibly carries a resolved memoryEnabled and optional template inputs; this is distinct from current server-side Chat retrieval.
facts.limits: Current official product documentation says local Cowork does not use shared Chat memory. Retained branch inputs are not evidence that local shared-memory behavior is enabled.

facts.claim: Project detail has org/project cache scope, optional placeholder data, and separate knowledge/settings/member permissions.
Project instructions are saved as prompt_template through project PUT; the editor guards duplicate save and supports view-only mode.
Projects distinguish doc text, uploaded files, and connector sync sources, with separate list/mutation contracts.
Document list may request compact metadata and per-document detail; compact listing is not proof that content was deleted.

The inspected project document contracts support create, single delete and bulk delete with list/detail/totals maintenance; bulk removal uses identity arrays. They do not establish an independent existing-document edit/update operation.

The connector refetchInterval returns false for absent, non-array or empty lists. Nonempty lists poll every five seconds while a sync is pending, otherwise every five minutes; transition out of pending triggers knowledge refresh.
Knowledge-search admission combines a client flag, capability check where applicable, and project-specific KB stats. Only then does tool construction include project_knowledge_search.

Knowledge capacity uses general search eligibility gh(), not the per-project use_project_knowledge_search decision. If general eligibility passes it uses the remote budget; otherwise it uses rounded 90 percent of the largest returned model hard_limit, with a fallback when no hard_limit exists. Missing text token estimates use ceil(content length / 4).
facts.limits: Client capacity/UX accounting is not the server tokenizer, ranking algorithm, or proof that every file is fully injected.

facts.claim: Project editing checks settings permission, knowledge editing permission, and member-management permission independently.
The styles search finds a compatibility menu enum, not a verified current chat Custom Styles CRUD implementation.
facts.limits: A shipped enum is not proof of a displayed menu, nor proof that a feature is globally removed.

facts.claim: customStyles:chatFont is visual typography preference, distinct from language-model response style.
The inspected send telemetry hard-codes has_personalized_style false; telemetry is not a complete API or product specification.
Code output-style command has no-session, loading, unavailable, choose, match-name/label, and switch branches.

facts.claim: Feature names normalize to decimal unsigned 32-bit keys; __gb__ identifiers already carry their key.
facts.limits: This is key normalization, not encryption, authorization, proof of secrecy, or a reason to reverse-map opaque IDs.

facts.claim: Security-relevant feature keys are removed from local forced-feature overrides by a guard around setForcedFeatures.
facts.limits: Static defense observation only; no overrides were set or tested.

facts.claim: The feature wrapper distinguishes on/off/unknown and memoizes shared evaluations.

Remote structured configuration uses schema safeParse and bounded fallback reporting. Absence can return a wrapper fallback without parsing or diagnostics; a field fallback that validates need not produce a diagnostic. Only the failure path classifies absent, mismatch, fallback_rejected or threw and deduplicates the report.
Account capability resolver maps explicit available/platform/tier/admin/entitlement states and uses per-feature fallbacks when a verdict is absent.

UI capability wrappers expose distinct consumers: useEnabledForUser combines availability with the user preference; useAdminToggleState displays the forced policy value when policy-controlled and otherwise reads the organization setting. User preference, organization setting and forced policy are not interchangeable.
A static organization capability table declares dependencies, destination field/endpoint, destructive-disable and consent metadata, and RBAC entitlements.
Gated imports and translation catalogs carry build and organization identity; data from another build/org is not automatically applied.
A compatibility fetch path keeps bootstrap data while automatic network query is disabled and exposed refetch is a no-op.
Route normalization maps old desktop Code paths into canonical paths with platform conditions, exceptions, and a maximum four passes.

Bootstrap capability hydration keys verdicts by supplied organization. It keeps existing data when not invalidated, updated no earlier than module startup, not in the future and younger than one minute, instead of overwriting it with bootstrap. Missing usable identity/verdict invalidates only stale capability queries. Membership-mismatched responses are independently skipped by the subscription path. This is a hydration/invalidation rule, not a universal freshness check before every capability read.
facts.limits: Membership mismatch and absent verdict are different branches. This is client cache hygiene, not proof of server authorization or a universal active-organization refresh rule.

static_inventory.method: Babel inert AST, direct imported evaluators with conservative ancestor-function shadow exclusion; no target execution; import-graph reachability is not runtime reachability
limitations: Conservative ancestor-function shadow exclusion can undercount valid calls.
Only explicitly mapped evaluator wrappers and direct imported bindings are counted; dynamic keys and additional wrapper chains are unresolved.
Literal keys include configuration objects and experiments, not only Boolean flags.
HTML script/static/dynamic import reachability is a necessary module-level candidate path; it does not prove that a function executes or that a user is entitled.
Neither opaque IDs nor codenames are interpreted as future features.

literal_key_scope.literal_calls_and_unique_literal_flags: Nonempty StringLiteral arguments only; excludes one empty-string placeholder call.

styles_negative_search.conclusion: No classic chat-style CRUD chain recovered by these terms and reviewed consumers. This does not establish global feature absence.
